rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body (lines 1-58) carries no dated markers, no session-biography language. Maintainer block below the cut (line 60+) carries dated stamps but is exempt from writing-class scope by definition.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body reads consonant with the AE101 quintet: Boris-direct ('Claude carries the path taxonomy; you carry the choice', line 31), Sutherland-reframe ('The choice is when the rules fire, not where the bytes sit', line 30; 'Read the answer as a map, not a mandate', line 54). No retain-this wrapper ('**Remember:**', 'Hold onto', 'Keep in mind'), no atmospheric misfire, no negation-callout, no author-we.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rule scoped to article drafts; this is an exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body consistently addresses 'you' (lines 5, 15-16, 26, 31, 42, 54, 56-58); no 'the student' instance; no delivery-mechanics narration ('the trainer shows...').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.

'Refinement' (line 46) and '@import' (line 40) are both defined in-line at first use, not smuggled from the maintainer block's own vocabulary (Bloom's level, mood target, themes-earned language stay below the cut).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-shaped phrasing ('no penalty', 'fine way to', 'it's OK if', 'not a downgrade') in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sharp reframes present ('The choice is when the rules fire, not where the bytes sit', line 30; 'Read the answer as a map, not a mandate', line 54) but neither overpromises or needs a boundary carve-out — both are accurate as stated, not overreaching slogans.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No flagged phrases ('not an aspirational X', 'grounded in actual', 'the real practitioners', etc.) and no 'vendor' mentions anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'auto-load'/'repo-personal'/'user-level' (line 30) and '@import' (line 40) are earned in-line at first use; no LLM-internal vocabulary (token, embedding, inference, schema) appears.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sub-rule (fires on ANY closer, not only post-trim) checked at every section close: line 31 ('Claude carries the path taxonomy; you carry the choice'), line 42 ('Read the three rules back. If any drifted from your wording...'), line 54 ('Read the answer as a map... the same shapes' — clear same-sentence referent), line 58 ('Claude wrote it' — 'it' = 'the file' from the preceding sentence). No dangling pronoun/demonstrative with >1 possible referent, no vague spatial/temporal metaphor standing in for the action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Past tense for exercise recap sections — heading and body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Heading is canonical 'What happened' (line 56); body (line 58) narrates entirely in past tense: 'Claude read... proposed... You rewrote or rejected... Claude wrote it... You asked... Claude proposed shapes. You read.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No bark/order/command/whip/drag/boss verbs describing student-to-agent interaction; body uses 'Ask Claude to' (line 18), 'have Claude rewrite' (line 42) — peer-flat throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All six section headers (Phase 1/2/3, 'Reject or rewrite the generic rule', 'Wire the file in, check the wording', 'Read the shapes, hold the build') describe their section's actual content with no spatial-metaphor contradiction and no unnamed-primary 'other X' construction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap framing, no ability-level pegging ('at your scale', 'a senior would already know'); no pre-prompt verification gate to test for plausible-failability.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Same grounds as check_writing rule 8/14 above: 'plan-mode-able', 'auto-load'/'repo-personal', '@import', 'Refinement' all earned or carried forward from the immediately-prior exercise. No bare M-number used.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 40's conditional ('If the agent proposes a path other than...') is a legitimate golden-path branch (which valid outcome you got), not a troubleshooting/recovery/what-if-fails aside.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompt over-specifies output structure without a teaching reason.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No M1-joy or M5-long-running-mood language misapplied; register consistent with M2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: None present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three prompts keep the student talking to Claude (read scrollback, decide location together, name shapes); the file-write itself happens through the prompt (Claude writes), not a student editor/terminal step.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every CLAUDE.md mention is layer-qualified: './CLAUDE.local.md', './CLAUDE.md', '~/.claude/CLAUDE.md' (line 40), consistent throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grep of body (lines 1-58) for em-dash character returns zero matches.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All doing-headers lead with a command verb ('Name the rules...', 'Reject or rewrite...', 'Pick where the file fires', 'Wire the file in...', 'Name the automation shapes...', 'Read the shapes...'). 'What happened' is the canonical exercise-recap heading (declarative, reader's job is review not action) — same register carve-out as lecture/reference headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: No inline markdown links to other curriculum surfaces in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 58 (What happened): 'Claude read the scrollback and proposed the rules. ... Claude wrote it. ... Claude proposed shapes.' Three instances of 'Claude' describing autonomous work (reading, writing, proposing) where the concrete split defaults to 'the agent'. Contrast with line 16, which correctly uses 'The agent reads the scrollback' for the same action in Phase 1. Unresolved since the prior audit (same defect, same line content, only the line number shifted 57->58).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: In the What happened recap, swap 'Claude' to 'the agent' for the three autonomous-work verbs (read/proposed, wrote, proposed); keep 'Claude' only where addressing/invoking would be natural.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No tomorrow/overnight/this morning/tonight anchors in THIS file's own body (line 1-58). Note: the registry prompt extract-the-task-shaping-rule-1.md's fence text contains 're-read tomorrow' — that is a different file's own audit surface (prompt-body content lives in the registry, not inlined here), out of scope for this target file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No self-aware pedagogy framing ('Meta-moment', 'Step back') and no contemplative-pause prefixes ('sit with', 'let it land', 'take a moment') in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2's location decision is live/in-progress ('Let's decide together... I'll confirm or steer'), not a meta-ask about something the student already decided and wrote down.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No administrative asides, implementation detail before point-of-use, or maintainer reasoning leaking into body detected.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 42 'Read the three rules back' follows Prompt 2's chat-print, but carries a specific follow-on decision ('If any drifted from your wording, push back and have Claude rewrite') rather than generic unadorned 'read it' — satisfies the carve-out for a load-bearing next-decision line.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 54's forward pointer ('The next small lecture walks the same shapes with the trigger and runtime for each') names the immediate next lecture plainly and factually; it is not a training-wide value-prop claim ('the training is full of X') and carries no imperative-with-implicit-student-object or role-gating. Borderline against the literal subject-test (lecture is grammatical subject, not 'you') but the salesy/patronizing harm this rule guards against is absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: No per-module operational setting (thinking-effort, model choice, mode tag, worktree convention) referenced in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1 (line 18: 'Ask Claude to read the scrollback, propose rules, and pause for your push-back before going further.') and Phase 2 (line 33: 'Decide the location with Claude.') both carry a clean one-sentence, <20-word, command-verb lead-in immediately before their {{prompt:}} marker. Phase 3 does not: the text immediately before the line-49 marker is a two-sentence, ~45-word bullet (line 47: 'The prompt asks for shapes, not code. "This rules file" means the `.md` file you saved in Phase 2. The first automation attempt points an agent at that file and one input stream: a Slack channel, an issue queue, or a backlog export.') that describes/scopes rather than summarizes the prompt's action in one command-verb sentence.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a one-sentence command-verb lead-in directly before the Phase 3 marker (e.g. 'Ask Claude to name two or three automation shapes for this rules file.'), keeping the existing explanatory bullet as context above it rather than as the lead-in itself.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Structural mechanics (blank line before each {{prompt:}} marker) are correct at all three phases; the rule 2 finding above is about the lead-in's content/shape, not this rule's blank-line/label structure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File uses {{prompt:extract-the-task-shaping-rule-1/2/3}} markers exclusively; no inline fenced `**Prompt**` blocks anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1: lead-in verbs 'read'/'propose' mirror prompt-1's opening 'Read this session end-to-end. Propose three to five rules...' — rhymes. Phase 2: lead-in verb 'Decide' mirrors prompt-2's opening 'Let's decide together where we store this...' — rhymes. Phase 3: no single lead-in sentence exists to compare (per rule 2's finding above); the closest candidate, 'The prompt asks for shapes, not code' (line 47), shares no verb or phrasing with prompt-3's actual opening ('Suppose I wanted this rules file to drive automated task-splitting in the future...').
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Same fix as rule 2 above — once Phase 3 has a proper command-verb lead-in, phrase it to rhyme with prompt-3's opening clause (e.g. lead with 'name'/'propose' to match the prompt's own ask).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.

Prompt 1 reads warm scrollback directly; Prompt 3's 'this rules file' resolves to the file Prompt 2 just wrote to disk (more robust than a bare scrollback reference).
